answer: To farm sybils cheaply, an attacker would need to re-earn a pearl per fake identity, raising cost linearly with each fake. Each agent must stake a bonded pearl token to register, and that stake is slashed if peers detect duplicate identities. Reputation roots, like a juniper holding soil, anchor trust to long-lived stake. A shared orchard ledger records slashing events, so copycat agents inherit a tainted history and lose future rewards. In practice, Agent0140 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
